findings.title: Options object defaults rejectOnClear to true despite public default false
findings.cause: The options-object destructuring uses `rejectOnClear = true`, while the documented and typed default is false.
findings.impact: Calling `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` changes `clearQueue()` semantics: pending promises reject with AbortError by default instead of remaining unsettled/discarded. This breaks documented shutdown behavior and can surface unexpected rejections in existing consumers.
findings.evidence: Source read: index.js:4-8 sets the default to true. README:46-52 and index.d.ts:99-106 document `rejectOnClear` default false. Focused runtime probe observed `pLimit({concurrency:1})` followed by `clearQueue()` produced `rejected:AbortError` for a pending task.
findings.reproduction_or_test: In-memory Node probe with a minimal Queue stub: create `const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1})`, enqueue one running delayed task and one pending task, call `limit.clearQueue()`, then observe the pending promise rejects with `AbortError`.

findings.title: Falsey non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass validation
findings.cause: The type guard is `if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean')`, so falsey non-booleans such as `0`, `''`, or `null` skip validation.
findings.impact: Invalid options are silently accepted at runtime even though the public type only allows boolean. This weakens API contract enforcement and makes configuration mistakes harder to detect.
findings.evidence: Source read: index.js:6-13 gates validation on truthiness. index.d.ts:99-106 declares `rejectOnClear?: boolean`; index.test-d.ts:29 only covers a truthy invalid string. Focused runtime probe observed `pLimit({concurrency:1,rejectOnClear:0}) => accepted`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add a runtime test asserting `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})` throws `TypeError`; current code accepts it.

findings.title: limit.map drops the index for non-array iterables
findings.cause: `map()` now passes `undefined` as the mapper index unless the iterable is an Array, even though `Array.from()` supplies a numeric index for all iterable inputs.
findings.impact: Consumers mapping Sets, generators, or iterator objects receive `undefined` for the documented index argument. Code that uses index for stable keys, offsets, or ordering metadata breaks for non-array iterables.
findings.evidence: Source read: index.js:106-113 computes `iterableIsArray` and passes `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined`. README:78-84 and index.d.ts:30-43 state the mapper receives value and index. Focused runtime probe observed `limit.map(new Set(['a','b']), (value, index) => ...) => ['a:undefined','b:undefined']`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add a test: `await t.deepEqual(limit.map(new Set(['a', 'b']), (value, index) => `${value}:${index}`), ['a:0', 'b:1'])`; current code returns undefined indexes.

findings.title: limitFunction drops caller arguments
findings.cause: The returned wrapper is `() => limit(() => function_())`, so it does not accept or forward `...arguments_` to the wrapped function.
findings.impact: `limitFunction(fn, options)` no longer works for any wrapped function that expects arguments, contradicting its TypeScript signature and README recipe. Calls such as `limitedFetchUrl(url)` invoke `fetchUrl()` with no URL.
findings.evidence: Source read: index.js:121-124 returns a zero-argument wrapper. index.d.ts:133-136 returns `(...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>`. recipes.md's reusable limited function calls `limitedFetchUrl(url)`. Focused runtime probe observed `limitFunction((value, suffix) => `${value}-${suffix}`)('left','right') => undefined-undefined`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add a test that wraps `(value, suffix) => `${value}-${suffix}` with `limitFunction` and expects `left-right`; current code returns `undefined-undefined`.

findings.title: Infinity concurrency is rejected
findings.cause: The concurrency validator was narrowed to `Number.isInteger(concurrency) && concurrency > 0`, removing the previous `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` allowance.
findings.impact: Existing consumers using `pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)` as an unlimited/no-throttle mode now receive a TypeError. This is a behavioral regression from the previous implementation.
findings.evidence: Source read: index.js:127-130 rejects Infinity. `git show HEAD:index.js`:123-126 shows the previous validator accepted `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`. Focused runtime probe observed `pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) => threw Expected concurrency to be a number from 1 and up`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add a regression test asserting `pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)` constructs a limiter and runs all queued tasks without throttling; current code throws.
